name: Pears in Spiced Wine Syrup
description: PLACEHOLDER example recipe. Whole pears poached in red wine with honey and warm spices, served in their reduced syrup. Replace with your own tested version.
ingredients: 12 firm pears (Bosc or similar), peeled with stems left on
directions: Combine the wine, water, honey, spices and orange peel in a pot large enough to hold the pears standing up. Bring to a simmer and stir until the honey dissolves.
Add the pears, cover with a round of baking parchment, and poach gently 25 to 40 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Turn them once so they colour evenly.
Lift the pears out to a dish. Boil the liquid hard until reduced to a syrup that coats a spoon, about 20 minutes. Strain out the spices.
Pour the syrup over the pears. Serve warm or chilled; they keep two days in the syrup and improve.
source: Placeholder; after 'Wardonys in syrup', Harleian MS 279 (c. 1430)
notes: PLACEHOLDER: quantities and timings are illustrative and untested. Contains alcohol; a cider or grape-juice version is easy for a dry table.
period_notes: Pears (wardens) stewed in wine with spices are a common 15th-century English dish; the originals colour the syrup with sanders (red sandalwood) and use mulberries or 'sugar' alongside honey.
